name: weather_forecast
description: Get a full weather analysis for a city — temperature, feels-like, humidity, wind speed AND direction, precipitation chance AND volume, pressure, all with real local timestamps. Use 'at_hour' (0-23, local time) for an accurate single reading closest to a specific time of day (e.g. 'weather at 3pm' -> at_hour=15) instead of a vague block. Use 'hours' for a short-term forecast window (e.g. next 5 hours) or 'days' for a multi-day outlook (e.g. tomorrow = days=1). If none of at_hour/hours/days is given, returns the nearest available data (~15 hours).

city.description: The name of the city to get the weather for.

at_hour.description: A specific local hour to check, 0-23 (e.g. 15 for 3pm). Returns the single closest 3-hour forecast bucket to this time, clearly labeled — OpenWeather's free tier resolution is 3 hours, so this is the closest available reading, not necessarily exact to the minute. Use with 'day_offset' for a day other than today.

day_offset.description: Used only with 'at_hour'. 0 = today (default), 1 = tomorrow, 2 = day after, etc., in the target city's local time.

hours.description: How many hours ahead to forecast as a block, e.g. 5. Rounded up to the nearest 3-hour interval internally (OpenWeather's data granularity). Use 'at_hour' instead if the user wants one specific time, not a range.

days.description: How many days ahead to forecast, e.g. 1 for tomorrow, 3 for a 3-day outlook. Use this instead of 'hours' whenever the request is phrased in terms of days (tomorrow, this weekend, etc.).
